100 of the 110 torso shapes that have an FMA class also have an open BodyParts3D mesh (998 element files from the 99 percent reduced PART-OF zip, 2,222,680 source faces; zip sha256 pinned, not committed). The page ships them decimated by vertex clustering to 148,060 faces (952 KB gzip) and transformed into the CT frame. The other 10 are mostly structures BodyParts3D does not mesh as a class (e.g. thyroid, colon, left auricle).

Frame mapping found by looking at sides, not guessed: BodyParts3D is +X patient-left, +Y posterior, +Z up (mm); the CT scene is +X patient-right, +Y up, +Z posterior. CT = (-x, z, y) of BodyParts3D. An automatic search over all 48 signed axis permutations picked a wrong mapping (scale 0.65, median 59 mm) because matched centroids are noisy; reading the left kidney and sternum positions fixed it.

Similarity fit on vertex-mean centroids of trunk structures, 6 rounds dropping the worst 20 percent: scale 0.9397 (this subject's trunk is about 6 percent smaller than the BodyParts3D body), rotation 10.6 degrees (forward head and stooped posture), 67 structures in the final fit. First round was scale 0.646, median 58.7 mm; last round median 31.1 mm on the fitted set.

Mean surface distance after the fit (2,500 points each way, seed 7): vertebrae 10.8 mm median (C4 5.0, C5 5.1, C6 6.9, sternum 6.9), ribs 26.4, lungs 25.1, organs 31.4, heart 15.6, skull 15.8. 27 structures are 'close' (under 15 mm), 56 'partial' (15 to 40 mm), 17 'far'.

The 17 'far' structures are expected failures, not bad meshes: skin (BodyParts3D is whole body, the CT is trunk and head), femurs and humeri (raised arms, cut legs), iliac arteries (263 mm: BodyParts3D runs them down the legs), carotid, subclavian and brachiocephalic arteries (neck posture), spinal cord (different extent), bladder and prostate (organ position varies with fill and posture), rib_right_9, iliac_vena_left.

A global similarity fit cannot model posture. The CT subject has raised arms and a forward head; a per-bone or articulated fit (the v4 H-Anim joints) is the right next step, and would shrink the limb and neck residuals.

Chamfer distance compares point clouds of two different people's anatomy. A small value means the shape and place agree; it is not a measure of error in either mesh, and BodyParts3D meshes are reduced to 1 percent of the original polygons.
